message.content: In the 19th‑century canon, **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss”** (1888–1891) stands out as the most celebrated and widely reproduced sculpture of that era. It captured the Romantic fascination with intimate emotion and became a cultural touchstone—its image has been replicated in countless editions, parodies, and homages worldwide. While other works such as Rodin’s “The Gates of Hell” (begun 1880) were monumental, “The Kiss” achieved the highest level of public recognition and enduring fame during the 1800s.
